text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Britain's envoy on Cyprus Sir David Hannay prepares for face-to-face talks between the leaders of the two sides in June.
- An icon starts to weep in a fourth church in the space of a month.
- The government holds Turkey responsible for Grey Wolves plans to storm into the fenced-off area of Famagusta.
- The United States insists on a compromise on Cyprus.

- The U.S. seeks new compromises. U.S. Ambassador Kenneth Brill says the two sides must give up their traditional positions on the dispute, while Britain's envoy Sir David Hannay raises the issue of a new constitution.
- Turkish Cypriots dwindle to 10.8 percent of Cyprus's population.
- Parties start laying down their conditions for partnership during the presidential elections next year.
- Trade unions warn they will order their members to go on strike if shopping hours are extended by one hour.
- Britain is working behind-the-scenes to produce a framework solution to the Cyprus problem.
